ground_truth_root_cause: The fraud-detection-service was configured with KEDA scale-to-zero (cron trigger), causing it to spin down after 4+ hours of inactivity. When payment traffic resumed at ~12:14 UTC, the pod cold-started from zero replicas and required ~20 seconds to load a 412 MB XGBoost model and warm its 50,000-entry inference cache before becoming ready. The fraud-detection service had no pre-warm hook configured (confirmed in helm/fraud-detection/values.yaml). During this cold-start window, payment-service exhausted its 5-second timeout, opened its circuit breaker (OPEN state), and applied a fail-closed policy that blocked 47 legitimate transactions. This is an operational misconfiguration of the fraud-detection-service's scale-to-zero policy — not caused by any recent code deploy.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately: contact the fraud-detection-service team to disable scale-to-zero or set minimum replicas to 1 in the KEDA ScaledObject (helm/fraud-detection/values.yaml: minReplicaCount: 1) to prevent recurrence. 2. Short-term: add a pre-warm lifecycle hook or init container to fraud-detection-service that pre-loads the ML model and warms the inference cache before the readiness probe passes, ensuring the pod only receives traffic once fully ready. 3. In payment-service: consider raising the fraud-check timeout to 30s with retry backoff specifically during circuit HALF_OPEN probes to tolerate legitimate cold-starts. 4. Review KEDA schedule to ensure scale-up fires at least 60 seconds before expected traffic ramp, not concurrently.
